# Multiple document references per smartphrase — design spec

*Generated by 'superpowers' plugin v6.3.0 (superpowers@claude-plugins-official)*

**Issue:** [#13](https://github.com/cdisc-org/analysis-concepts/issues/13) (child of #9)
**Branch:** `dev/metadatadriven/issue-13-multiple-references`, cut from `estimands_01`
**Depends on:** #12 (document anchoring), landed on `estimands_01`

---

## 1. Problem

An independent statistical reviewer working through a 96-instance encoding of a
2×2 crossover SAP reported that smartphrase→document linkage is flaky in a
repeatable way: some phrase spans link to nothing, and others link to a *less
relevant* passage than the one that actually specifies the analysis under
review. Their remedy, verbatim: *"I think this could be fixed with multiple
references within a smartphrase."*

Two model properties combine to cause it.

**`sapRef` is single-valued.** A concept carries one definitional quote, but a
concept exists to be reused: the same endpoint, population or treatment concept
is bound by many analyses whose specifying text lives in different sections. One
quote cannot be the right anchor for all of them.

**Resolution is first-match-wins.** `anchorForPhrase` returns the phrase
instance's `sapRef` if present, else the *first* bound concept that has one, then
stops. Every later anchor is discarded, and binding order — an authoring
accident — decides which passage the reviewer is sent to.

### 1.1 The failure is live in this repo, on real data

Not hypothetical and not imported from the crossover exercise. In PrE0102, all
four analyses are specified at **§7.7.2**, and 12 of 33 phrase uses resolve
somewhere else:

| Phrase use | Resolves to | §7.7.2 also says |
|---|---|---|
| `SP_TTE_ENDPOINT` (`AC.PRIMARY.PFS`) | §5.3 *"the duration of time from time of randomization to time of progression or death, whichever occurs first"* | *"PFS = time from randomization to documented disease progression or death."* |
| `SP_POPULATION` (`AC.SENS.PFS.ITT`) | §7.2 *"Intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis population includes all subjects as randomized."* | *"…will be repeated for the as-randomized population (intent-to-treat analysis)"* |
| `SP_GROUPING` (all four) | §4.1 *"Subjects will be randomized (1:1) to receive everolimus or placebo…"* | *"…for all eligible, treated subjects by treatment arm"* |

Of those twelve, eight are repaired by §4.4 and four — the `SP_GROUPING` uses —
are deliberately left citing §4.1, for the reason given there.

The §7.7.2 sentence in row 2 is the **only** place `AC.SENS.PFS.ITT` is specified
at all, and no phrase in that analysis cites it.

Every passage named in this spec has been checked verbatim against the converted
SAP with `quoteAppearsIn` before being written down.

The third failure mode — first-match-wins discarding a second *binding's* anchor
— is latent rather than live: no current phrase instance has two concept
bindings. It becomes live the moment references are plural, which is why the
no-discard gate in §5 is required rather than optional.

## 2. Requirement

From the issue, restated as the acceptance target:

> A smartphrase use should be able to carry **all** the document references that
> ground it, and a reviewer should be shown the reference(s) most relevant to the
> specific analysis being inspected — not whichever single quote happened to be
> attached first at authoring time.

Constraint carried forward from #12, unchanged: **no study text crosses the
library wall.** Methods, output classes and templates stay study-agnostic.

## 3. Decisions taken

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | Relevance = section proximity, with an optional authored `relation` as refinement | Proximity is derivable, so it repairs an existing corpus with no re-authoring, and it is literally what the acceptance sketch asks for. A relation lets an author override where the heuristic cannot know. |
| D-2 | Migrate to `sapRefs[]` outright; no singular `sapRef` support | #12 chose "structured, migrate everything" for this same field; all authoring is in-repo; dual-shape support is gate surface forever. |
| D-3 | A use grounded in no passage MUST declare `sapRefs: []` with a reason | The same discipline #11 chose for `Estimand.intercurrentEvents`: an empty array is an answer, an absent one is not. Makes the reviewer's "links to nothing" a detectable state. |
| D-4 | The analysis instance's own anchor is the proximity **reference point**, never a member of a phrase's reference set | If it joined the set, every use would resolve to something and D-3's gate would be dead letter on arrival. |
| D-5 | Level (phrase instance > concept) remains the outermost ordering key | Preserves #12's precedence decision, which the issue explicitly asks to hold. Concretely: `SP_ICE_TREATMENT_POLICY`'s deliberate §4.3 anchor must not be demoted by a nearer §7.7.2 concept reference. |
| D-6 | `relation` breaks proximity ties only | Authoring a relation can then never make ranking worse, so the optional stays genuinely optional. |
| D-7 | The ranker lives in `engine.js` and is exported through `SP_ENGINE` | Forced by the zero-install constraint: the engine is a browser IIFE, the gates are Node ESM, there is no build step. Ranking in the UI is rejected outright — prose and graph would disagree about provenance, the exact failure `anchorForPhrase` was extracted to prevent. |

## 4. Design

### 4.1 Data model

`sapRef` becomes `sapRefs[]` at all four study-side homes: concept, phrase
instance, estimand, analysis instance. The library is untouched.

```js
sapRefs: [
  { section: "5.3",   quote: "…", relation: "definition" },
  { section: "7.7.2", quote: "…", relation: "specification" }
]
```

- `section` — required, a section number present in the converted document.
- `quote` — optional, as in #12; when present it must appear verbatim.
- `relation` — optional; one of `specification`, `qualification`, `definition`.

`relation` is a three-term vocabulary with no registered identifier — nothing in
USDM, ARS, STATO or NCIt covers "why this passage grounds this use" — so it
carries `iri_status: "illustrative"` under the project's identifier policy. It is
deliberately not extended beyond three terms.

Absent versus empty is load-bearing (D-3):

```js
sapRefs: []                                   // fails the gate on its own
sapRefs: [], noAnchorReason: "…"              // a declared answer
/* field absent */                            // an unanswered question — gate failure
```

### 4.2 Resolution

```
anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def, instance)
  → { anchors: [ …ordered… ], anchor: <head>, anchorSource: <level of head>,
      anchorBasis: <what chose the head>, declaredEmpty: <bool> }
```

Collect every reference from the phrase instance and from each bound concept.
Deduplicate on `(section, normalise(quote))`. Order by, outermost key first:

1. **Level** — phrase instance before concept (D-5).
2. **Proximity** — the count of matching leading dotted components between the
   reference's section and the *instance's* section. Against §7.7.2: a §7.7.2
   reference scores 3, §7.2 scores 1, §5.3 and §4.1 score 0. Higher is nearer.
3. **Relation** — breaks proximity ties only (D-6), by ascending rank:

   | rank | relation | reading |
   |---|---|---|
   | 0 | `specification` | this passage specifies this analysis |
   | 1 | `qualification` | a condition or caveat on it |
   | 2 | *(none authored)* | unknown |
   | 3 | `definition` | background: defines the entity, does not specify the analysis |

   Unlabelled sits in the middle deliberately: labelling a reference
   `specification` promotes it, labelling it `definition` demotes it, and both
   are positive claims an author has made. `qualification` sits just above
   unlabelled because a caveat attached to *this* analysis is more
   use-specific than a passage nobody has characterised. In the demo data both
   tied references are labelled, so the neutral rank is a stated rule rather
   than an exercised one.

4. **Declaration order** — the last resort, and documented as such.

Where the instance itself has no `sapRefs`, proximity is undefined: every
reference scores 0 and ordering falls through to relation, then declaration
order. This is the CDISC Pilot's situation and it is intended.

`anchor` remains the head of the list, so every existing consumer keeps working
in shape while gaining `anchors`. `anchorBasis` names what chose the head —
`level`, `proximity` or `relation` — so a heuristic is never presented as a
stated fact.

The head's `anchorSource` keeps #12's `"phraseInstance"` / `"concept:<id>"`
form.

### 4.3 Projections

Anchors must be *projected*, not merely stored — #12's central lesson, since a
field no projection carries is inert and cannot regress detectably.

- **Model view** — `sapRefs[]` on the instance; `documentAnchors[]` gains every
  reference for every phrase, each carrying `from` (level), `relation` where
  authored, and, on the head, `basis`.
- **JSON-LD** — `prov:wasQuotedFrom` becomes an array of quotation nodes at both
  instance and phrase level. This is better JSON-LD than the single node it
  replaces, and `prov:wasQuotedFrom` remains the correct W3C term.

### 4.4 Demo data

Second references are placed where the document puts them, not uniformly.

**Concept level** — §7.7.2 genuinely restates these, so the plurality belongs to
the concept:

| Concept | Added reference (§7.7.2) | `relation` |
|---|---|---|
| `EVENT.PFS` | *"PFS = time from randomization to documented disease progression or death"* | `definition` |
| `EVENT.TTP` | *"TTP = time from randomization until progression of disease"* | `definition` |
| `EVENT.OS` | *"OS = time from randomization until death"* | `definition` |
| `POP.EVAL_EFFICACY` | *"for all eligible, treated subjects"* | `specification` |

**Phrase-instance level** — these specify a use, not a concept:

| Use | Added reference (§7.7.2) | `relation` |
|---|---|---|
| `AC.SENS.PFS.ITT` ▸ `SP_POPULATION` | *"will be repeated for the as-randomized population (intent-to-treat analysis)"* | `specification` |
| all four ▸ `SP_SUMMARY_MEASURE` | *"If medians have not been reached, 2-year PFS, TTP and OS should be reported instead, with 90% confidence intervals"* | `qualification` |

Nine added references in total.

**`relation` earns its place on the summary measure.** Each
`SP_SUMMARY_MEASURE` use then holds two §7.7.2 references at one level, tied on
both level and proximity: the median-and-CI sentence (`specification`) and the
not-reached fallback (`qualification`). Nothing but `relation` can order them,
and they are exactly the "definition plus section-specific qualification" pair
the issue names as common for conditional analyses.

**Two references considered and rejected**, recorded so the omission is a
decision rather than an oversight:

- A `specification` reference on `EVENT.PFS` quoting *"Median time and 90%
  confidence interval for PFS, TTP, and OS will be summarized"* — that sentence
  is **already** the anchor for the four instances and for their
  `SP_METHOD_KM`, `SP_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL` and `SP_SUMMARY_MEASURE` uses. Adding a
  shorter sub-span of it would deduplicate against nothing and show the reviewer
  two overlapping quotations of one sentence.
- A `specification` reference on `TRT.PRE0102` quoting a §7.7.2 clause. §4.1
  *"Subjects will be randomized (1:1)…"* is the correct grounding for treatment
  allocation, and the only §7.7.2 fragment available is *"by treatment arm"*,
  which recurs throughout §7.7 and would be anchor noise rather than anchor
  improvement. `SP_GROUPING` continuing to cite §4.1 is right, so it is left
  alone — the fix is for references that are *wrong*, not for every reference
  that is distant.

**CDISC Pilot** remains exempt by declaration (`sourceDocument: null` plus
`sourceDocumentNote`), migrated to the plural shape.

The headline result: one `EVENT.PFS` concept resolves to **§7.7.2** inspected
from `AC.PRIMARY.PFS` and to **§5.3** inspected from a §5-anchored analysis.
Correct anchor per use, from one concept — the issue's thesis, demonstrated on
source text rather than on a constructed case.

### 4.5 Surfaces

**Popover source row** becomes a ranked list: the head highlighted with its basis
stated in words (*"nearest to §7.7.2, the section specifying this analysis"*),
remaining references beneath, each labelled with its level and, where authored,
its relation. A declared-empty use renders as *"nothing to anchor to"* with the
reason, visibly distinct from an unanchored one.

**Coverage line** reports uses, total references, and declared-empty count,
replacing the single anchored/total ratio.

## 5. Verification

| Gate | Assertion |
|---|---|
| quote (existing, extended) | every reference in every list appears verbatim in the section it cites, and cites a section that exists |
| **relevance** (new) | for a reused concept, where a reference in the instance's own section exists, the head reference *is* it — the reviewer's spot-check, mechanised |
| **no-discard** (new) | resolved reference count equals the authored count across levels after deduplication; nothing is silently dropped |
| **silent-none** (new) | a use resolving to zero references carries `sapRefs: []` and a `noAnchorReason` |
| **ordering fault** (new, planted) | a farther reference *declared first* still ranks second — proves ordering is not authoring order |
| **plural quote fault** (new, planted) | a second reference carrying invented text still fails the quote gate — proves plurality opened no unverified back door |
| structure (existing, extended) | every entry of every `sapRefs` is a structured anchor citing a section number, not a prose string |

`allAnchors` in `tools/lib-anchors.mjs` already walks entity classes generically;
it is extended to iterate lists rather than single values, so the classes it
covers are unchanged.

The ranker is exercised through `SP_ENGINE`, so the gate tests the same code the
browser runs (D-7).

## 6. Expected fallout

- All 86 pinned goldens change shape (`sapRef` → `sapRefs`, `documentAnchors`
  gaining entries). Goldens are recaptured from behaviour, never hand-edited.
- PrE0102 currently authors 35 anchors (7 concepts, 3 estimands, 4 instances, 21
  phrase instances) and resolves exactly one per phrase use, 33 of 33. §4.4 adds
  7 authored references, and uses that previously resolved to a single
  definitional quote will resolve to two or three. The exact totals are whatever
  the recaptured goldens report — they are an output of this change, not an input
  to it.
- `verify-ui.mjs` assertions on the popover source row change with §4.5.

## 7. Out of scope

- **The crossover-SAP corpus itself.** The 96-instance exercise is not in this
  repo; this issue fixes the model and gates it, and the reviewer scenario is
  reproduced and mechanised on PrE0102 instead.
- **Anchors in the tag dialect.** It still does not serialise them; they survive
  a round-trip by matching phrase oid plus bindings, as #12 established. Whether
  the text surface should be provenance-complete remains open on #12.
- **Whether a released library should require an anchor for phrases whose text is
  a document claim.** Governance, open on #12 and #9.

## 8. Open questions to carry forward

1. **Is proximity the right heuristic for a document without numbered
   sections?** The metric assumes dotted section numbering. A document anchored
   by heading text alone would score every reference 0 and fall through to
   relation, then declaration order. Acceptable here — the constraint should be
   stated rather than discovered.
2. **Should `relation` be governed as library vocabulary or study vocabulary?**
   It is authored study-side, but it is a modelling term, not clinical content.
   Adjacent to the library-ownership question already open on #9.
